subject: Borealis performance run — next steps & k6 handoff
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.inference.com>
To: Maya Chen <maya.chen@borealis-systems.com>; qa-team@borealis-systems.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Jan 2028 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Borealis performance run — next steps & k6 handoff

Hi Maya / Borealis QA team,

Thanks for the call this morning — helpful to sync on the performance goals and customer-led run. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Goals (as discussed)
- P95 latency: <= 180ms for single-turn text generation (50-token avg)
- Sustained throughput: 2500 reqs/min for the non-streaming endpoint
- Streaming concurrency: support 120 concurrent streaming sessions with average 20 token/sec output
- Start/end guardrails: 10s cold-start SLA for pinned models, KV-cache warmup expected in first 5 minutes

Customer-led run details we agreed to hand off:
1) Borealis will run k6-based traffic against our hosted test endpoint during the window you propose.
2) You'll provide k6 scripts + a driver configuration (we requested the script naming standard so our ops can map to pods).
3) We will provide a scoped test account + IP allowlist entries and a temporary access token.
4) Redwood SE will monitor logs, metrics, and remain on the call to triage issues; we'll capture token-level latency & token-count breakdowns.

Immediate asks from Redwood:
- Please attach the k6 scripts and the test plan (ramp, steady-state, and teardown timings).
- Confirm your preferred 2-hour window in PST (we suggested 2028-01-12 14:00-16:00 PST) or propose an alternate.
- Provide IP ranges for your runner machines so we can add to the allowlist.

Ben / Soojin — can you prep:
- a scoped test API key and a read-only metrics dashboard link (Datadog)
- an ops runbook snippet for our side to follow if we hit token-exhaust or KV-cache thrash

Maya — if the plan above looks right, please reply with scripts + preferred window and IPs.

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
log an.wright@redwood.inference.com
+1 415 555 0123

Attachment: borealis-k6-scripts-v1.tar.gz (contains k6 entrypoint + data files)

From: Maya Chen <maya.chen@borealis-systems.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.inference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: qa-team@borealis-systems.com
Date: Wed, 11 Jan 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Borealis performance run — next steps & k6 handoff

Thanks Logan — solid recap. We attached the initial k6 bundle and a short test plan (high-level). Summary from our side: 

What we attached:
- borealis-k6-scripts-v1.tar.gz (k6 scripts + README)
- borealis-test-plan-20280112.pdf (ramp, steady-state targets, expected error thresholds)

We confirm target window: 2028-01-12 14:00-16:00 PST works for our QA engineers.

IP ranges for our runners (these come from our CI fleet):
- 34.223.112.0/24
- 54.162.45.128/26

One question for Redwood: do you have a separate ingestion endpoint for streaming probes or should we target the same streaming endpoint used in demo? We plan to exercise both non-streaming and streaming code paths in this run.

We'll also need the scoped API key and the allowlist entries added ~24 hours before the test window.

Thanks,
Maya Chen
Head of QA | Borealis Systems
maya.chen@borealis-systems.com
Attachment: borealis-k6-scripts-v1.tar.gz

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference.com>
To: Maya Chen <maya.chen@borealis-systems.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.inference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Jan 2028 10:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Borealis performance run — next steps & k6 handoff

Heads-up on the ops bits we've prepped:
- Scoped API key: BOR-TEST-2028-01 (will expire 2028-01-13 00:00 PST) — sending credentials to your QA mailbox after we confirm allowlist additions.
- Streaming endpoint: use streaming-test.redwood.inference.com:443 (same TLS certs as prod; rate-limits lowered during your run).
- Non-stream endpoint: api-test.redwood.inference.com/v1/generate

Notes on test profile mapping (from k6 bundle):
- We mapped k6 group "stream_sessions" to our streaming concurrency buckets. Expect our autoscaler to spin up pods by concurrent-session count; please avoid >150 simultaneous new sessions in the ramp phase.
- The "text_gen_burst" scenario peaks token rates; set VU arrival pacing to avoid single-spike storms.

I'll add the IP ranges to the allowlist today (ticket INF-5921) and paste the ticket link once it's live.

Ops runbook highlights (short):
- If error-rate > 2% sustained for 5 minutes, reduce VUs by 30% and call out to Redwood SE channel.
- If p95 exceeds 500ms for >3 minutes, we will throttle bursters and capture heap traces for triage.

I'll follow up with the dashboard link.

Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.inference.com
Attachment: (none)

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.inference.com>
To: Maya Chen <maya.chen@borealis-systems.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Jan 2028 07:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Borealis performance run — next steps & k6 handoff

Perfect — thanks all. Quick coordination notes for the call and run: 

Pre-run (12 Jan morning)
- Redwood will add IP ranges: ticket INF-5921 (Ben to paste link).
- Redwood to create BOR-TEST-2028-01 key and DM creds to maya.chen@borealis-systems.com after allowlist is live.
- Soojin will publish a read-only Datadog link by 11:30 PST so QA can watch traces/latency buckets live.

Run-day steps (14:00 PST start)
- 14:00 — ramp to 60% in 10 minutes
- 14:10 — ramp to steady-state 100% target (as per test plan)
- 14:40 — 5 minute spike test to 130% to validate autoscaler and fallback policy
- 15:30 — start graceful teardown; validate token-count billing snapshot

Post-run deliverables
- Redwood will send a raw metrics dump (token-level breakdown + p50/p95/p99) and failure logs within 4 hours.
- Mutual action item: if any regression is detected, we'll triage with a joint RCA within 48 hours.

Maya — we'll join your call at 13:50 PST for final preflight. Ben / Soojin — please be on standby for any rapid rollbacks.

Cheers,
Logan

Attachment: none

From: Maya Chen <maya.chen@borealis-systems.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.inference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Jan 2028 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Borealis performance run — next steps & k6 handoff

All set on our side. INF-5921 looks good (we see the allowlist entries). QA will kick off the run at 14:00 PST; Maya + two engineers on the call. We'll DM the test logs to the shared channel and pull the dashboard. Appreciate Redwood joining the preflight at 13:50.

See you shortly,
Maya

Attachment: borealis-test-plan-20280112.pdf
